title: Price Extra Arms and the monk third hand after the arm count
description:
Closes #1

Phase 6 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p6` (`0a1ab3529`): one documentation commit and the plan's record of
the phase. No code changes: `docs/guides/PLAYER_RACES_REFERENCE.md` is the only place the
prices live, and no race grants Extra Arms.

## Audit of feat 1320 and 1321 grants

Production has run the arm count since the 2026-10-04 release (`d5cd6a735`), so the item's
pre-deploy check became an audit of live data, done read-only as the game user on 2026-10-08:

| Where | Extra Arms (1320) | Four Arms (1321) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| World objects: `APPLY_FEAT` affects (33 in all, development and production alike, by the recipe in the plan) | none | none |
| World mobiles: `Feat:` and `MFeat:` lines (1659) | none | none |
| Production player files (7428), their `Feat:` sections | none | one, a level 30 Thri-Kreen: the race's own innate |
| Production `player_save_objs` (509487 rows), `pet_save_objs` (1), `player_save_objs_sheathed` (0), `object_database_bonuses` | none | none |
| Production `house_data` (7951 rows, 44 houses), the table `House_load()` reads | none | none |
| Production `lib/house` and `lib/plrobjs` files, which the game opens only to see that a record exists | none | none |
| The same on the development copy (7097 player files, 489375 rows, 9743 house rows) | none | none |

Nothing changed meaning for anyone: no character, pet, house or object carries Extra Arms, and
Four Arms gave the same four arms before the count as after it.

## Decisions

- Price by the arm a rank adds: the third arm 9 RP, the fourth 6 RP, each arm past four 1 RP.
  The split of Four Arms' 15 follows what each arm opens: the worn positions three to one (the
  lost-slot row the other way), and the weapon hands by their swings in `plan_second_pair()`,
  five candidates to four at level 30 with haste, the fourth hand's last three behind the
  two-weapon feats, so the 11 RP of weapon hands split 6 to 5.
- Mixed sources: a race is priced by the arm count it ends with, whatever mix of Four Arms,
  Extra Arms ranks and `arm_adjust` produces it, since `arm_count()` is the only count the game
  reads. A negative `arm_adjust` is a drawback by the lost-slot row (one arm or none: the cap).
- The single-trait cap exemption stays Thri-Kreen's Four Arms alone (composition rule 2). A
  third arm is over the cap in every tier but Epic quest, and four arms fit only there, so
  another race taking arms records its own exemption in that rule.
- The monk's empty third hand is the swing a weapon there makes: `plan_second_pair()` plans one
  third-hand chain, set by either, and gives the monk no candidate of its own; the fourth hand
  always needs a weapon. Class interaction, which the model does not price, so it is inside the
  15 RP and Thri-Kreen stays at 20.0 RP.

## Review

Two findings on the audit record, both fixed after the tag: `5b2917cd4` audits `house_data`,
the table the game loads houses from, and `f4c5c9624` makes the recorded world-file recipe take
two-field and CR-terminated `A` records and says that a prototype's own affects never reach
`serialized_obj`. Neither changes the result.

## Verification

- `pre-commit run mdformat` on the changed files passes.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (216 s) on
  `429ce84b6` and again on `f4c5c9624` (218 s); the format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass
  again on each record commit.

title: Save a sheath's weapons with a pet and extract them with the sheath
description:
Closes #17

Phase 5 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p5` (`bfaaa8799`): two code commits, each with its test, a test
commit, and the plan's record of the phase.

## Cause

A sheath's weapons hang off `sheath_primary` and `sheath_secondary`, and nothing else holds
them. Only the player save (`player_save_objs_sheathed`, rows under the owner's name) and the
`sheath` / `unsheath` commands handled them.

- `objsave_save_obj_record_db_pet()` wrote no sheath rows, and a pet has no rows under an
  owner's name anyway: a loaded sheath given to a pet came back empty when the pet was restored,
  and its weapons were in no row.
- `extract_obj()` did not look at them: junking or selling a loaded sheath, and the extraction
  after a rent save, freed the sheath and left the weapons in `object_list` with no holder.
  After a rent save their rows were written, so that was a leak only; after a junk or a sale
  they were gone from play without having been destroyed.

## What changes

`59bc44f45`: `extract_obj()` extracts what a sheath holds, beside the loop that extracts a
container's contents. Nothing nulls the pointers afterwards: the sheath is freed in the same
call. `Test_object_extraction_takes_a_sheaths_weapons` (no database) extracts a sheath holding
two weapons and finds `object_list` as it was; without the change the two weapons stay.

`2b8959cdd`: `Crash_save_pet()` writes a sheath's weapons as the pet's own objects beside the
sheath, through the pet record writer, as `House_save()` does for a house: no new table and no
migration. A worn sheath's weapons are written at `MIN(0, location)`, as inventory records,
since `pet_object_graph_valid()` refuses two records on one wear position and with them the
whole set; a carried sheath's are written at its own depth, so a sheath in a bag puts its
weapons in the bag. The restored pet carries the weapons and an empty sheath.
`Test_pet_save_stores_a_sheaths_weapons_as_its_own` (database) saves a pet with a worn sheath
holding a blade and a shield and a carried sheath holding a dagger through `pet_save_objs()`
and loads it through `pet_load_objs()`: five rows, one of them with a wear position, and the
restored pet wears an empty sheath and carries the other sheath, empty, and the three weapons.
Without the change the save writes two rows.

`4a9bd579b`: the pet test also refuses a weapon's row, the blade's and then the shield's; each
attempt fails the save, as any refused row does, and leaves the records written before it. The
first matrix run had left those two failure lines uncovered.

`docs/systems/SAVE_SYSTEMS_BREAKDOWN.md` has the pet rule, in the pets section.

The plan's check before the change held, with nothing to change: `overwrite_object()` keeps a
target's own sheath pointers (phase 7), every writer's temporary object comes from
`read_object()` or `create_obj()`, and the editors free their copies with
`free_object_strings()`, never `extract_obj()`.

## Found while building

The leak #17 describes never showed in the memory-check or sanitizer jobs, and could not have:
a weapon left behind stays on its rnum hash chain, so valgrind and LeakSanitizer count it as
still reachable. `Test_house_save_stores_a_sheaths_weapons_as_its_own` is clean under valgrind
with and without the fix; it no longer extracts its weapons by hand, since the teardown's
extraction of the sheath takes them. The extraction test watches `object_list` instead.

## Verification

- Both new tests fail on the code of `0b88bb81d`: the extraction test with the two weapons still in
  `object_list`, the pet test with 2 rows written instead of 5.
- The two new tests, the house sheath test and the refused-row save test are clean under
  valgrind, with the database on.
- `make -j16 test` on `4a9bd579b`: 2055 tests pass. `make install` done.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, on a database freshly built from `sql/master_schema.sql`:
  2055 of 2055 pass.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master` on `2b8959cdd`: 33 of 33 jobs pass
  (522 s); the unit, sanitizer and memory-check jobs run 2055 tests each. The persistence changed
  lines were 4 of 6 covered, above the floor, the two uncovered being the refusals `4a9bd579b`
  then covered.
- On `4a9bd579b`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (256 s); the unit, sanitizer and memory-check jobs run 2055
  tests each, and the persistence changed lines are 100% covered.
- The format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on `bfaaa8799`, which adds the plan's record
  only.

## Not in this merge request

- The player sheath loader's debug trace (`SHEATH1` to `SHEATH6`, and the text of its
  `SELECT`) logged at every load: work item #33, seen while building and not changed here.
  `objs_from_sheath()`, which had no caller, went in the review round (below).
- `otransform`'s copy of a fresh object over the live one, which leaves the live object on its
  old rnum hash chain with the fresh copy's links and miscounts both prototypes: work item #34,
  pre-existing, seen while fixing the review findings.
- A sheath's weapons are not walked by `Crash_extract_norents()`: a rentable sheath keeps a
  no-rent weapon through a rent, as before.
- No deploy: the fixes reach production with the next release.

## Review round

Three findings, fixed one commit each after the tag; the plan's phase 5 section has the record.

| Thread | Commit | Test |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Stale sheath slot read through freed memory | `079e9bd6e` | `Test_gameplay_sheathed_weapon_extracted_alone_leaves_its_slot`, `Test_player_load_puts_a_sheaths_weapons_back_in_it`, `TestArmCountUnsheathChecksEachItem` |
| A sheathed artifact's destruction invisible to the ledger | `8a8f0fdd7` | `Test_artifact_integration_sheathed_instance_destruction_releases_ownership` |
| `delete_object()` destroys a deleted sheath's weapons and walks into one freed | `da68e251a` | `Test_gameplay_object_delete_hands_a_sheaths_weapons_to_its_wearer` |

A sheathed object now knows its sheath (`sheathed_in`); `obj_to_sheath()` and `obj_from_sheath()`
in `src/core/handler.c` set and clear the slot and the back-pointer together, at every site.
`extract_obj()` takes a sheathed object out of its sheath as it takes an object out of a room,
a character or a container; `artifact_on_extract()` counts a sheathed object as placed; and
`delete_object()` hands a deleted sheath's weapons to its holder beside the contents.

Verification, on `da68e251a`: the first gameplay test fails on `bfaaa8799` with the reviewer's
valgrind read at `handler.c:3098`; the artifact and delete tests fail on `079e9bd6e` with only
their test applied, the delete one with the walk reading the freed dagger under valgrind. The
sheath, artifact and renumber tests are clean under valgrind with the database on; `make -j16
test` passes 2059 tests; `./cutest` with the database tests on, on a fresh
`sql/master_schema.sql` database, passes 2059 of 2059; the local matrix: 33 of 33 jobs pass (1431 s); the unit, sanitizer and memory-check jobs run 2059
tests each, the persistence changed lines are 100% covered and the olc changed lines 75%, both
above their floors, and the clang-tidy gate has no finding. The
format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on the record commit.

title: Take a leaving character's bagged objects along with the rest
description:
Closes #16

Phase 4 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p4` (`0a662d23a`): three code commits, each with its test, and the
plan's record of the phase.

## Cause

`extract_char()` called `empty_bags_to_inventory()` (`src/core/handler.c`), which only unlinked
each bagged object: nothing put it in the inventory and nothing extracted it, so it stayed in
`object_list`, held by no one, after its owner left the game. It passed bag number 1 to
`obj_from_bag()` for all ten bags, so the move it reported named bag 1. The leaving save
(`objsave_save_and_extract()`) wrote the bags but extracted only the worn and carried objects.

The plan's check before the change failed: nothing kept a carried object from being dropped in
the room on a leave without a save and loaded again from the last save. `extract_char_final()`
calls `Crash_delete_crashfile()` for that, which deletes a crash save's file, but under
`OBJSAVE_DB` (always defined in `src/obj/objsave.c`) it returns at once and the rows stay. A
crash-saved carried and worn gem, then a purge: both lay in the room and both rows were still
there. So the bags could not simply follow the carried objects, and that defect is fixed first.

## What changes

`d989a8517`: once `extract_char_final()` has dropped anything in the room, it writes the
character's object save again. The character holds nothing by then, so the rows, the header and
the file all come out empty, and the next login does not bring back what the room holds. A
character that left with a rent, idle or cryo save holds nothing at that point, and its save
stands. The `Crash_delete_crashfile()` call there goes. Making that function work under
`OBJSAVE_DB` instead would also delete the crash save at every death, its other two callers,
where the character keeps all its objects (`make_pc_corpse()` moves none).
`Test_leaving_without_a_save_drops_everything_and_keeps_no_object_save` covers it.

`be819da53`, the bags:

- `extract_char_final()` takes each bagged object out of its own bag and puts it in the room, as
  it does the carried and worn ones. The move names the bag. `empty_bags_to_inventory()` goes:
  a stop in the inventory would report a move from bag to inventory, which the quest system
  counts as finding the object, and the bus dispatches it at once, to a character that is
  leaving.
- `objsave_save_and_extract()` extracts each bag's objects after the worn ones;
  `extract_obj()` already takes an object out of its bag.
- `Test_leaving_saves_keep_the_bags_and_take_them_along` replaces
  `Test_cryo_and_idle_saves_keep_what_is_in_the_bags`, which took its bagged gem out by hand: a
  cryo save leaves the bags and `object_list` empty, and a load from the saved rows puts a gem
  back in bag 1 and one in bag 3. The leave without a save now has a gem in bag 1 and one in bag
  3: both end in the room, each moved there from the bag it names.

`0980ae2dc`, found while building: `do_sort()` (sortto, sortfrom) and `do_bags()` read the bag
storage of whoever runs them, and a mobile has none (`bags` is NULL). `command_interpreter()`
lets a mobile run any command below immortal level, so either command ended the server in a
segmentation fault. Both now answer "You have no bags."
`Test_gameplay_bag_commands_refuse_a_character_without_bags` covers both.

`docs/systems/SAVE_SYSTEMS_BREAKDOWN.md` says what the leaving saves take along and what a leave
without a save does.

`0a662d23a`: the plan's record of the phase.

## Verification

Before the changes:

- The leaving-save test failed with the bags still full after the cryo save.
- The test without a save found one object of three in the room; with the bags fixed it still
  found every row. On `d989a8517` alone its first form fails without the change, both rows left.
- The bag-command test ends in SIGSEGV without either of its two checks.

On `0980ae2dc`:

- `make -j16 test`: 2051 tests pass.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, first run on a database freshly built from
  `sql/master_schema.sql`: 2051 of 2051 pass.
- The three tests are clean under valgrind, the two leaving tests with the database on.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (1476 s); the unit,
  sanitizer and memory-check jobs run 2051 tests each, and the persistence changed lines are
  100% covered.
- The format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on `0a662d23a`, which adds the plan's record
  only.

## Not in this merge request

- `Crash_delete_crashfile()` and its two calls at death stay: a no-op under `OBJSAVE_DB`, which
  is right there.
- The duplicate-login cleanup in `perform_dupe_check()` extracts a second in-game copy of a
  character; if it held anything, its empty save replaces the save of the copy that stays until
  that copy is saved again. The code says no such copy should exist.
- If the empty save cannot be written, the last save stands and the dropped objects come back at
  the next login, as before; the writer logs it.
- No deploy: the fixes reach production with the next release.

title: Keep a live object's own links and lists when another object is written over it
description:
Closes #30

Phase 7 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p7` (`73eaa93e5`): one code commit with its tests, and the plan's
record of the phase. The review found five defects. Two code commits after the tag fix all five,
and a last commit records the review.

The branch starts at `object-save-fixes-p3`, the head of MR !25 at the time, because phase 3 was
still in review and both phases edit the plan and `src/olc/genobj.c`. The review of phase 3 found
the `char_sdesc` double free below on its own and fixed it in `ddacf712f`, with the same line;
that commit is merged into this branch (`15f66c7c9`). MR !25 was merged on 2026-10-06
(`5fd630349`) and master is merged into this branch (`16b1abdf5`), so this merge request shows
phase 7 alone.

## Cause

Two functions in `src/olc/genobj.c` wrote one whole `struct obj_data` over another and then put
back a list of the target's runtime fields: `update_all_objects()`, for every live object of a
prototype that OLC saves, and `copy_object_main()`, for the editor copies. Each list was older
than fields the struct has gained.

After an OLC save of a prototype, each live object of it

- pointed at the prototype's special abilities and spellbook. `free_obj()` frees both with the
  object, so extracting one live object freed the prototype's lists under it and under the other
  live objects;
- had lost its hash links while still on its `obj_rnum_hash` chain, and its sheath pointers,
  trap, group-loot link and pending limb slot;
- had dropped its own strings, arcane mark and restring identifier without freeing them.

The iedit commit wrote back the hash links, sheath pointers and trap the object had when the
edit began.

## What changes

`584524ec5`, handed to review:

- `overwrite_object()` is the one place that says what a target keeps when another object is
  written over it: where it is, what holds it and what it holds, its list, hash and registry
  links, its events and transfer state, its sheath pointers and trap, and the other runtime-only
  fields. `copy_object_main()` goes through it, and the iedit commit's own restore list is gone.
- `give_obj_own_copies()` is the part of `read_object()` that gives an object copies of its own of
  its prototype's arcane mark, restring identifier, spellbook and abilities.
- `index_object()` clears the slot a new prototype goes into, and `oedit_setup_existing()` clears
  its edit copy, since a copy keeps the target's runtime fields.
- Fixed in the same commit: an edit copy shared `char_sdesc` with the live object and both freed
  it (the line is also phase 3's `ddacf712f`), and a new prototype kept the event and registry
  fields of whatever its slot held.

`8e7b0b073`, review:

- `adjust_objects()` and `delete_object()` move each renumbered live object to the hash chain of
  its new rnum. They left it on the old chain, and the next `read_object()` into that bucket wrote
  into a freed object.
- Both skip objects with no prototype. `delete_object()` gave such an object a bogus rnum that
  `extract_obj()` used as an `obj_index` subscript. A notice board with no object stays NOTHING.
- `remove_obj_from_rnum_hash()` leaves a chain the object does not head alone. A mail letter or
  forged note has rnum 1 on no chain (#31), and removing it emptied that bucket.
- `delete_object()` frees the deleted prototype's strings and trigger list.

`dd9732777`, review:

- An OLC save gives each live object the new prototype's definition field by field where the
  object still held the old prototype's, and keeps what it has of its own, as a reload from a save
  would. Before, a save of a carrier prototype rewrote every generated weapon and armour in the
  game, and any save took restrings, arcane marks, scribed spellbook pages, an essence's level and
  a resized item's size. `add_object()` keeps the old prototype until the live objects are done.
- The save no longer drops a live object's script while it stays registered for random and time
  triggers, which read the object after it was freed. `overwrite_object()` keeps the target's
  script.
- A live target of `overwrite_object()` keeps its rnum, the key of its hash chain.
- A save and an iedit commit carry a change in an object's weight to its containers and carrier,
  as `obj_to_obj()` counts it.
- The save frees the old prototype's trigger list and each live object's own.
- `MAX_TEST_CASES` rises from 2048 to 4096: the suite has 2049 tests.

## Tests

All in `unittests/CuTest/test_gameplay_e2e.c`:

- `Test_gameplay_object_prototype_save_leaves_live_objects_whole`: two live objects, one restrung,
  marked and with a weapon in its sheath; the edit adds an ability and a spellbook page. Each
  object has lists of its own, the hash chain and the sheath pointer are as they were, the
  restrung object keeps its name and mark, and extracting one leaves the prototype and the other
  whole.
- `Test_gameplay_object_editor_copy_leaves_each_object_its_own_links` and
  `Test_gameplay_object_new_prototype_takes_nothing_from_its_slot`.
- `Test_gameplay_object_renumber_keeps_the_hash_and_unnumbered_objects`
- `Test_gameplay_object_prototype_save_keeps_what_each_object_made_its_own`
- `Test_gameplay_object_overwrite_keeps_weight_totals`
- `Test_gameplay_object_prototype_save_extracts_live_scripts`
- `Test_gameplay_object_copy_keeps_a_live_targets_rnum`

## Verification

- Each test fails on the code before the change it covers: the first three on `8556f9ca8`, the
  last five on `6a55903f5`, where the renumber test ends in a segmentation fault.
- The 11 object tests are clean under valgrind.
- On `dd9732777`: `make -j16 test`, 2049 tests pass. `./cutest` with the database tests on, first
  run on a database freshly built from `sql/master_schema.sql`: 2049 of 2049 pass.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master` on `dd9732777`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (577 s), the olc changed lines 99.39% covered. The format,
  hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on `55189ee1c`, which adds the plan's record only.

## Not in this merge request

- An ability list or spellbook that still matched the old prototype is replaced by a copy at a
  save and given up, not freed: #29's preview copy shares the lists of the object it previews,
  and an open iedit copy shares its spellbook. #29 has to end that sharing first; a note on #29
  says so.
- An ability or spellbook page the builder edits in place reaches the live objects at their next
  load, not at the save: the oedit copy shares those lists with the prototype, so the old
  prototype already shows the edit when the save compares.
- #31: mail letters and forged notes take rnum 1 without being objects of that prototype.
- No deploy: the fix reaches production with the next release.

title: Free the arcane mark of an object with no prototype
description:
Closes #15

Phase 3 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p3` (`8556f9ca8`): two code commits, each with its test, and the
plan's record of the phase. After the tag: the review's one finding, fixed in `ddacf712f`, and
the plan's record of the review.

## Cause

`free_obj()` sends an object with no prototype through `free_object_strings()`
(`src/olc/genobj.c`), which freed every string the object owns except `arcane_mark`.
`free_object_strings_proto()`, the path of an object with a prototype, has always freed it. So
an unnumbered object lost its mark's memory when it was extracted: the file and player-row
loaders give such an object a mark from its `AMrk` line, and the arcane mark spell gives one to
any object.

## What changes

`79a3c99ed`: `free_object_strings()` frees `arcane_mark`.

Its other callers were checked for a double free. Each frees the object or writes over it
afterwards, and each of those objects owns its mark or has none:

- `add_object()` copies the edited object over the prototype, and `copy_object_main()`
  duplicates the mark.
- The OLC cleanup (`src/olc/oasis.c`) and the iedit commit (`src/olc/oedit.c`) free an edit copy
  whose mark `copy_object()` duplicated. The iedit commit leaked that copy's mark the same way,
  and no longer does.
- The spec test fixture frees a prototype from `parse_object()`, which reads no mark.

The prototype teardown in `destroy_db()`, which #15 names, frees by hand and does not call the
function.

Tests:

- `Test_object_saves_bind_player_house_and_serialized_text` no longer frees its two marks by
  hand before `extract_obj()`. It needs a database, and the memory-check job has none.
- `Test_object_without_a_prototype_frees_its_arcane_mark` needs none: it saves and loads a
  marked object through the file loader, compares the mark and extracts both objects.

`a0757112c`, found while checking those callers: `copy_object()` sent every target through
`free_object_strings_proto()`, which compares the target's strings with its prototype's. For a
target with no prototype that read `obj_proto[-1]`; the iedit commit reaches it with any live
object that has no prototype. It now chooses the free function as `free_obj()` does.
`Test_gameplay_object_editor_copy_frees_an_object_with_no_prototype` copies over such an object
with no prototype table at all.

`8556f9ca8`: the plan's record of the phase.

## Review

One finding: `copy_object_strings()` duplicated every string `free_object_strings()` frees
except `char_sdesc`, a corpse's description of the fallen, so an `iedit` of a corpse made an edit
copy that shared it with the live corpse and the commit freed it twice. `ddacf712f` duplicates it
and extends `Test_gameplay_object_editor_copy_frees_an_object_with_no_prototype` to a target and
source with a `char_sdesc` each; the test fails on the shared pointer before the change. Phase 7
(MR !26) had met the same double free and carries the same line; its branch has `ddacf712f`
merged in, so it merges cleanly after this one.

## Verification

Without the fix (`free_object_strings()` as on master, both tests in place):

- Under valgrind each test loses its two marks.
- Of the matrix, `test-memory-check` fails on the new test's two blocks and
  `test-sanitizers-gcc-address-undefined` reports all four.
- The `copy_object()` test ends in SIGSEGV before `a0757112c`.

On `a0757112c`:

Phase 2 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at

title: Load a saved special ability that has no command word
description:
Closes #19

Phase 1 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p1` (`ab7a35b84`): two code commits and the plan's record of the
phase. The review had one finding; its fix and the plan's record of the review are the two
commits after the tag (`1d904677a`, `c62c01124`).

## What changes

- **A saved ability with no command word loads again** (`ea33ddd29`). The object writers store
  an ability as seven numbers and its command word, and the word is empty for an ability that
  fires on hit or on a critical hit. `objsave_replace_special_ability()` required eight fields,
  so the file, player and sheath loaders logged `Invalid SpAb record` and left the object with
  what its prototype gives it (nothing, for an object with no prototype), and the pet loader
  rejected the pet's whole object set. The parser now accepts seven numbers and leaves the
  command word NULL, as `parse_object()` does for a prototype's seven-field record. Fewer than
  seven numbers is still rejected.
- **The record replaces one ability, not the list** (`1d904677a`, the review finding). The
  writers store an object's first ability only, and the loader freed the whole list before it
  installed that record. While the seven-number record was rejected, a prototype-backed object
  kept its prototype's list; accepting it cut the three prototypes with two real abilities
  (#1213, #1244, #20621) to their first one at every load. The record now replaces the ability
  of its kind, or else the first one, and the rest of the list stays. A first ability that has
  a command word keeps the rest too, which it did not on master.
- **`utter` passes over an ability with no command word** (`1340e6957`, found while building).
  `process_weapon_abilities()` and `process_armor_abilities()` passed a NULL command word to
  `strcmp()`, so any uttered word crashed the server while such an object was wielded or worn.
  A prototype's seven-field record or a builder's edit could already produce that ability; the
  loader fix adds saved objects, so the guard comes first.

## Tests

- `Test_object_special_ability_without_a_command_word_survives_save_and_load`: the production
  record's ability (vampiric, level 30, on hit and on critical hit) is saved and loaded through
  the file loader always, and through the player-row and pet-row loaders when the database tests
  are on, and compared field by field. It fails before the fix with the record logged by each of
  the three loaders.
- `Test_object_special_ability_record_keeps_the_rest_of_the_prototype_list`: the two abilities
  of #1213 (Bane, Flaming Burst on `ignitus`) through the file loader always and the player-row
  loader when the database tests are on; then with the prototype's list the other way round, as
  after an OLC save of the zone; with a first ability that has a command word; and with an
  ability of a kind the prototype does not have. It fails on the loader of `ab7a35b84`, and on
  the fix when that matches by position only or puts an unmatched ability in front of the list.
- `Test_pet_object_decoder_validates_fields_and_preserves_text`: a six-number record is one more
  rejected payload.
- `Test_gameplay_utter_passes_over_an_ability_with_no_command_word`: `utter` with such an
  ability on a wielded weapon and on worn armor. It ends in SIGSEGV before the guard.

## Verification

On `1d904677a`, the last code commit:

- `make -j16 test`: 2039 tests pass.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, against a freshly loaded disposable `mariadb:10.11`
  built from `sql/master_schema.sql`: 2038 of 2039 pass. The one failure is
  `Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent`, the test of #18 (phase 2), on
  the kind of database #18 describes; this branch does not touch it.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (357 s), the
  memory-check, sanitizer and coverage jobs among them. The format, hygiene and secrets jobs
  pass again on `c62c01124`, which adds the plan's record only.

## Not in this merge request

- The writers still save an object's first ability only, so a change to another ability, an
  emptied list, and the later abilities of an object with no prototype do not survive a load.
  That is older than this merge request and needs a new row format: #28.
- `downgrade` and `applyoil` drop ability lists without freeing them, and `downgrade` leaves its
  preview object behind. Seen while tracing the review finding: #29.
- An ability already lost from a saved row is not restored: a row that lost its line cannot be
  told from a row that never had one.
- No deploy. After the next release the `Invalid SpAb record ... 61 30 48 0 0 0 0` line should
  no longer appear in the production log.

title: Vessels S15: checked vessel purchases and payouts
description:
Closes #14

S15 of the vessel study (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`, Phase 15), the last step: the
vessel commands that take or pay gold now write and check both stores inside the command, the
captain's gold in the player file and the ship's side in MariaDB. Before, the ship's side was
written at once and the gold moved in memory only, so a crash before the next per-minute save
kept a purchase and gave its gold back, or took a sold item and never paid.

Review range: `vessels-s15-base..vessels-s15` (the S14 close-out `16c6611fb` comes first; the
plan is `c295d6aa8`, the build `aec826b19`, the gate step `6a1ada514` and `77cc74137`, the
fixes found before hand-off `bc2a45b69`). Review round 1 is on top, `vessels-s15..feat/vessels-s15`:
see the last section.

## What changes

- **A purchase takes the gold first.** `vessel_charge()` checks that the database answers, saves
  the debit with `save_char_checked()` and refuses the purchase when either fails, before
  anything aboard has changed. If the ship's side then cannot be written, it is put back and the
  gold is returned (`vessel_refund()`). If the put-back cannot be written either, the purchase
  stands and stays paid (review round 1).
- **A payout writes the ship's side first**, then pays and saves. A payment that cannot be saved
  takes the gold back and puts the item back, in memory and in the rows. If the put-back cannot
  be written, the sale stands and the gold is paid in memory ("undone" is never said of a sale
  the rows still hold).
- **Seven shipyard jobs** (`shiphire`, `shipweapon buy`, `shipequip buy`, `shiprearm`, dock
  `shiprepair`, `shipupgrade`, `shipchristen`) copy the hull before they change her;
  `vessel_purchase_recorded()` writes her with the new `vessel_save_hull()` (interior row,
  runtime state, weapons, owner, crew, refits, each checked) and on a failure restores the copy,
  writes her back and refunds. `shipweapon sell` and `shipequip sell` use
  `vessel_sale_recorded()`.
- **`shipbuy`** charges, then spawns; a failed spawn (it rolls itself back) refunds. The rollback
  deletes her rows before it takes her out of play; when they cannot be deleted she stays in
  play and stays paid (review round 1). The spawn writes the runtime row last, so a crash in
  mid-spawn leaves rows that hold the slot at boot, not a hull. **A trade-in** charges what is owed before the fittings are
  counted, rebuilds and saves, then pays for the fittings; a hull that cannot be rebuilt or
  recorded, or a payment that cannot be saved, undoes the rebuild (`vessel_trade_in_undo()`: the
  new interior reclaimed, the hull restored from the copy, her old rooms recreated as boot
  recreates them). An undo that cannot be recorded keeps the charge for the staff to settle
  (review round 1).
- **`shipsummon`** saves the summons (the emptied manifest, then the hull as stowed, cast off
  and with her autopilot stopped) before she leaves the world or anything alongside or aboard
  is touched, so one that cannot be saved leaves her as she was; one that cannot be written back
  either stands (review round 1).
- **`bounty pay`, `marque`**: charge, then the row; when the write reports a failure the row is
  read back, and the fee is returned only if the row does not show the write.
- **`contractdeliver`**: the contract and the manifest in one transaction (sent once more after
  a `COMMIT` without a reply; both writes are absolute), then the payout. When neither the
  delivery nor taking it back can be confirmed, the captain and the staff are told.
- `shipupgrade` now saves the runtime row with the refit bit: the raised ceilings were in memory
  only until the next runtime save, so a crash kept "installed" without its points.

New code is in `src/vessels/vessels_payment.c`; the commands change in their own files.

## Where to look

- Outside a transaction, a statement sent on a connection that has just been lost does not fail:
  the library reconnects and sends it again. A single statement fails only with its reply lost,
  after the server ran it. That is why a refused purchase is **written back**, not only restored
  in memory, and why the admiralty's rows are read back.
- The undo of the shipyard jobs is `*ship = *before`. Nothing outside the struct changes between
  the copy and the restore at those seven sites; `shipchristen` renames the hull object and the
  rooms only after the write.
- `vessel_db_save_runtime()` saves a stowed hull's own location, not the room of a hull object
  that still stands (the summons is saved while it does).
- `vessel_save_one()` now fails when the owner, crew or refit write fails; it still attempts
  every part past the interior, runtime and weapon rows. `vessel_save_hull()` stops at the first
  failure.
- Two faults, left as they are and recorded: the bounty pay-off and `marque` return the fee when
  the write reports a failure and the row cannot be read back either.
- A database that does not answer refuses these purchases before the gold is taken; the tests
  that bought and sold in memory only now use the test database.
- Not S14's settlement record, as planned: a crash between a command's two writes still splits
  the stores, always against the player (paid and not delivered, or delivered and not paid).

## Verification

Everything below ran on `bc3f39c30`, whose code is `bc2a45b69`; the head `6c0975cd1` (the tag)
adds only the record of these results to the study and testing documents. Details are in the
Phase 15 section of the study document.

| Check | Result |
| -- | -- |
| `make test-all`, database cases on | 2,034 production tests and 32 protocol tests pass |
| New tests | `unittests/CuTest/test_vessel_payment.c`: four DB-backed tests on the real tables (the seven shipyard jobs, the two sales, the admiralty's fees, the delivery), each with a player file that cannot be saved and a ship-side write that is lost; cases for `shipsummon` in `test_vessel_loss.c` and for `shipbuy` and the trade-in's charge in `test_vessel_shipyard.c` |
| Vessel help verifier | 7 checks pass (64 content phrases) |
| SQL | none new |
| Live gates (private-namespace harness, dump reload) | 22 of 22 jobs pass, the economy gate also with every database session killed twice |
| Local CI matrix (`scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`) | 33 of 33 jobs pass |

No unit world generates ship interiors, so the refused hull write of `shipbuy` and of the trade-in
is played in the loss gate: the harness has the database refuse one design's runtime row (a CHECK
constraint), and Vesselmate, who owns only the gate's boat, buys a hull of that design and trades
the boat in for one. Both are undone, his purse is the same before and after, she is still a boat
with her owner and her bosun, and the gate's real trade-in then rebuilds the same hull.

Found and fixed before hand-off (`bc2a45b69`, recorded in `bc3f39c30`): an independent read of
the build found no single failed write that loses or duplicates gold or an item, and seven
narrower things, all fixed: a refused summons had already cast off, released vehicles and
stopped the autopilot; the summons wrote the stowed hull before the emptied manifest;
`vessel_save_one()` had begun to skip parts after a failed owner, crew or refit write; a
trade-in whose rebuild failed left the hull without an interior; a spawn's leftover rows could
become a hull at boot; a sale that stands did not rewrite the hull; a delivery with an unknown
outcome said too little. The first CI run failed clang-tidy on the tests' struct `memcmp()`.
The first version of the gate step traded in a harbor fixture of the staff character and was
moved into the two-character session.

## Review round 1

Four findings (one P2, three P3), each fixed in its own commit on top of the tag, range

| -- | -- | -- |

| P3 | A purchase whose write-back fails was called undone and refunded while her rows kept it | `c53d1601e`: the gold is returned only after a write-back that succeeded. A shipyard job and a summons stand and stay paid; the trade-in keeps the charge and tells the staff; `vessel_charge()` refuses uncharged when the database does not answer; a hull that makes port saves her manifest with her runtime row |
| P3 | A refunded `shipbuy` could leave a hull the next boot rebuilt | `c584bdab0`: the spawn's rollback deletes her rows first; when that does not commit she stays in play and stays paid |

`VESSEL_SYSTEM.md` follows in `94c3c5a9a`, the record in `bb9b86e3e`. No help entry changes.

title: Vessels S14: two-phase vessel settlements
description:
Closes #12

S14 of the vessel study (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`, Phase 14): a cargo trade, a
freight acceptance and a dock-fee payment are settled in two phases, so a crash between the
ship's side in MariaDB and the captain's gold in the player file no longer leaves one without
the other.

Review range: `vessels-s14-base..vessels-s14` (the S13 close-out `96b3af5a1` comes first; the
plan is `4ddf5f9ba`, the build `6bdce1e49`).

## What changes

- **Settlement row** (schema Phase 25, `vessel_settlements`). Written in the ship-side
  transaction, it carries the undo: signed deltas for the port's supply and the hold's lot, the
  contract to reopen, the dock fee owed again. Unique keys on `ship_id` and `player_id` hold a
  ship's and a player's accounts while one is open.
- **Player-file marker** (`VSet`, `GET_VESSEL_SETTLEMENT()`): the id of the newest settlement
  whose gold the file holds, saved with the gold.
- **Reconcile** (`vessel_settlements_reconcile()`), at login (from the insurance delivery every
  login makes), and as a gate at the start of `cargobuy`, `cargosell`, `contractaccept`,
  `contractdeliver`, `contractabandon` and `dockfees pay`: a row whose id is the file's marker is
  deleted; any other is undone from the row, with no gold moved. Another captain's row is judged
  from his player file, so a ship does not wait for an absent helmsman.
- **Unanswered `COMMIT`**: the row is read back with a locking read. When it cannot be read (or
  an undo cannot be recorded), the settlement is taken out of memory, the hull remembers its id,
  and her manifest is not written until a reconcile has settled it.
- `trade_settle()`'s "the trade stands and will be saved shortly" and the second write after an
  unanswered `COMMIT` are gone: the row settles both. "Undone" is said only once the undo is
  committed.

New code is in `src/vessels/vessels_settlement.c`; the commands change in `vessels_trade.c` and
`vessels_contracts.c`.

## Where to look

- `settlement_undo()` and `settlement_unresolved`: the one piece of in-memory state, and why
  `vessel_db_save_cargo()` refuses while it is set.
- "Covered" is `marker == id`, not `<=` as `VIns` and `VMer` use: with one open row per player
  the two agree, and equality does not depend on ids never restarting.
- The dock fee's undo is a restore (only when the hull owes nothing), not a delta: a runtime save
  rewrites the balance from memory at any time.

## Verification

The first round ran on `8ed5d8a3a`; what the later fixes touch ran again on `80f6d45e5`, the last

title: Vessels S13: transactions that survive a lost connection
description:
S13 of the vessel study: transactions that survive a lost connection.

Closes #13

## Problem

Every database connection reconnects by itself (`MYSQL_OPT_RECONNECT`). When one dropped inside a
transaction, the server rolled the transaction back, one command failed, and the statements after
it ran one by one in autocommit on a new session; a `COMMIT` among them reported success. An
object save left the old rows and the new partial ones together. A `COMMIT` whose reply was lost
was taken for a rollback when it may have committed. Work item #13 lists the sites.

Probing the client library with real drops before planning showed two things the item did not
have: `mysql_ping()` retries by itself and returns success on a new session, and the close of a
prepared statement can be the first command to meet the drop, so no statement fails at all.

## Fix

- **The rule lives in the query layer** (`src/database/mysql.c`), the only place that sends
  commands. A connection that lost its transaction is marked and takes no statement until the
  caller ends the transaction: `ROLLBACK` is sent, a `COMMIT` fails and is answered with a
  `ROLLBACK`, a new `START TRANSACTION` starts clean. Queries, prepared statements, the close of
  one, and pings all mark. The mark is kept on the handle (`MARIADB_OPT_USERDATA`), so it
  survives the reconnect and goes with the handle. No writer has to stop at its first failure.
- **`mysql_commit_transaction()`** tells a confirmed `COMMIT`, a refused one and one without a
  reply apart, and rolls back what is not confirmed. Cargo trades use it (`trade_commit()` is
  gone). After a `COMMIT` without a reply, pet storage and retrieval, a hull's change of owner and
  the end of a vessel event read the database back with a locking read, which waits for the lost
  session to finish.
- **Object and house saves.** The writers report a row that was not written. The save commits the
  rest, keeps `PLR_CRASH` or `ROOM_HOUSE_CRASH` so the next pass saves again, and tells the staff
  whose objects they were. `Crash_save_single()` no longer clears the flag after a failed object
  save. `Crash_idlesave()` commits. An extra description that does not fit a record is left out
  instead of the object (object, sheath and pet writers).
- **`house_data`** loses the unique key on `vnum` that let a house keep one object
  (`master_schema.sql`, `db_init.c`), with boot migration `2026100401`.
- **Smaller sites.** A bounty that cannot be read is not overwritten with the new offense. The
  help writers check inside their transaction that the session still holds the help
  synchronization lock. `hedit` deletes removed keywords.
- **The pool** reconnects a stale handle in place instead of closing the handle `conn` points at.

## Found on the way, fixed here

- `mysql_pool_acquire()` could hold the game while the database was away: it retired a connection
  that failed its check and, with none left and none to open, tried again without end on the
  game's one thread. It now returns no connection, which its caller already handles. Read from
  the code, not seen in production.
- `Crash_cryosave()` stored a frozen character's objects beside the last save's, with no
  transaction. It runs only where rent is not free.
- The rule itself: a caller that failed without ending its transaction would have left the
  connection refusing everyone's statements, and the query that loads a player's objects at login
  stops the server when it fails. All 26 transaction sites end theirs on every path, and the mark
  now lasts one game pulse at most: after that the layer rolls the transaction back itself and
  logs it (`3eab48d60`).
- The test database built from `master_schema.sql` had the `house_data` key: the new house test
  failed on it until the boot migration ran.

## Tests

The connection is really lost: `mysql_test_drop_connection_at()` shuts the socket down at a named
statement, before it is sent or after the server ran it. These tests write the real tables with
test-only rows, since a TEMPORARY table goes with its session.

- `unittests/CuTest/test_database_transactions.c` (new): the rule for a query, a prepared
  statement, a statement close and a ping; the helper's three results; the pool; a crash save and
  a house save lost at a row and retried; a row refused on a good connection; the idle, cryo and
  rent saves; the owner transfer, the event finish and the bounty; the help lock and `hedit`.
- `test_database_persistence.c`: the pet save lost at a row, the keeper's store and retrieve both
  ways, the longest record, the left-out extra description, the migration on the old table shape.
- `test_vessel_rewards.c`: the cargo trade test now loses its connection for real.

## Verification

On `3eab48d60`, the final source:

- `make test-all` with the database cases: 2,015 CuTest cases, the protocol harness's 32 and the
  Python suites passed; SQL interpolation within baseline.
- The boot migration ran for real on a test database built from the old definitions: the unique
  key was there before, gone after, and `idx_vnum` stayed.
- The local CI matrix (`scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`): all 33 jobs passed,
  clang-tidy with 0 findings; the changed lines are covered at 95.83% in the database layer and
  84.75% in persistence.
- All 20 live gates and provisioners in `scripts/vessels/` passed in the namespace harness on
  fresh reloads of the development dump.
- A live check of the layer: the economy gate passed while a second process killed the server's
  database sessions twice, and the server's log has no `SYSERR`.

The first CI run found a race in the test seam (the reply could arrive before the socket was shut
down) and two analyzer findings in the new tests; both are fixed in the commits here.

## Review round 1

Nine findings, each fixed in its own commit on top of `vessels-s13`
(`vessels-s13..feat/vessels-s13`); every thread has the details.

| | Finding | Fix |
| -- | -- | -- |
| P1 | A sheath holding a weapon in a house crashed the house save (older than S13) | `44b82187b`: the house stores the sheath's weapons as its own objects |
| P2 | Cryo and idle saves dropped the bag rows | `69ecda7a4`: both write the bags |
| P2 | Rent, idle and cryo saves left the objects in memory after a failed save, to be dropped in the room | `4c54755ce`: one writer for the four player saves; a leaving save is written a second time, then the objects leave memory either way |
| P2 | A deadlock's victim was not marked | `796f9a8a8`: error 1213 marks the transaction lost |
| P2 | An unreadable read-back was taken for a rollback: event scored twice, pets guessed | `263f76864`: the event's finish is idempotent on its own row; the pet keeper chooses no state until `pets restore` reads the rows |
| P3 | An incomplete save never set the crash flag | `5976699d8`: `PLR_CRASH` and `ROOM_HOUSE_CRASH` are set |
| P3 | `log_hint_usage()` freed an uninitialized pointer (older than S13) | `9ea0d4f94`: `mysql_pool_query()` clears the result first |
| P3 | `hedit` deleted another entry's keywords | `456000371`: a save under a tag the editor did not load is refused when that entry exists |
| P3 | A plunder's bounty was announced though not recorded | `1b4363645`: one retry; announced and passed on only when recorded |

`9a0e69438` brings the system documents in line, and the study document records the round.

One proposal was not taken: emptying a sheath on `remove`. The help entry `DRAW-WEAPONS`
documents carrying several loaded sheaths, and the house now stores the weapons, so nothing is
lost without it.

Verified on the final source (`1b4363645`): `make test-all` with the database cases (2,020 CuTest

title: Vessels S12: fixes from the post-merge review
description:
Fixes from a private review of MR !18, which merged without one (range
`vessels-s12-base..master`: S12, owned waypoints and routes, and S11's review round 2).

## Fixes (one commit each)

- `3996cb84b` **Keep a captain's waypoints and routes to that captain.** S12 let only a row's
  creator change it but let every captain use it. That coupled captains two ways: a captain could
  put another's waypoint on a route, and its creator could then never delete it; and a route's
  creator could change the course of another captain's hull scheduled on that route. A captain
  may now sail (`setroute`), schedule (`setschedule`), list, and route through only their own
  waypoints and routes and the harbors' (creator 0). Immortals may use any. Name lookups take
  the caller's own row, then the harbors'. An in-use guard on `addtoroute` was dropped as the
  alternative, because it would let a rival freeze your route by scheduling a hull on it.
- `9ab0bac74` **Give a removed player's waypoints and routes to the staff.** Boot sets
  `top_idnum` from the index, so removing the highest-numbered player hands that ID, and their
  rows, to the next new character.
- `2ad435a40` **Count Connector/C's 5000-range client errors (5013, 5014) as an unanswered
  COMMIT.**
- `d2218eb25` **Stop the manifest writer at a failure only inside a transaction.** `2ba35d6b1`
  made it stop at the first failure everywhere, which lost every later lot for callers that save
  without a transaction.
- `905184ab4` **Create `ship_waypoints` and `ship_routes` with `creator_id`.** Tables made
  through the staff `init vessels` path lacked the column until the next reboot.

Known and tracked, not changed here: the residual after an unanswered COMMIT whose second write

title: Vessels S12: owned waypoints and routes
description:
S12 of the vessel study: owned waypoints and routes.

Closes #11

## Problem

Vessel waypoints and routes recorded no creator, so any captain could delete another captain's
idle waypoint or route. Tracing it found a second hole of the same kind: `addtoroute` let any
captain append a waypoint to any route, and a scheduled hull rebuilds her route from that shared
cache at every departure, so a rival could change a public ferry's course, or disable her schedule
with a waypoint her route check cannot reach.

## Fix

- Schema Phase 24: `creator_id INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` on `ship_waypoints` and
  `ship_routes` (the player's ID; 0 for content and rows made before S12), with rollback and
  verifier SQL, `master_schema.sql`, and the same `ALTER`s at boot in
  `vessel_ownership_ensure_schema()`, which runs before the waypoints and routes load.
- `setwaypoint` and `createroute` record the player (an NPC records 0). `delwaypoint`, `delroute`
  and `addtoroute` allow only the creator or an immortal, before S10's in-use refusals, which stay.
  Using a route stays open to every captain.
- Every route and waypoint command resolves a name to the caller's own row first, so a rival's
  same-named row cannot lock a captain out of their own.
- Rows that predate the column keep creator 0 (nothing records who made them): only the staff
  change them. On the development database all three routes are content on schedules.
- Help (DELWAYPOINT, DELROUTE, ADDTOROUTE) in `help.hlp` and `help_vessel_entries.sql`, three new
  help-verifier patterns, `VESSEL_SYSTEM.md`, the player guide, and the testing docs.

## Tests

- `Test_vessel_waypoints_and_routes_answer_to_their_creator`: a mortal captain is refused another
  captain's and a content waypoint and route, reaches their own same-named route, and an immortal
  is not refused. S10's in-use test now runs as the creator.
- DB-backed `Test_vessel_waypoints_and_routes_record_their_creator`: the boot ensure adds the
  column to a pre-S12 table, the commands record the player, a reload reads the creator back,

title: Vessels S11: checked cargo trades
description:
S11 of the vessel study: checked cargo trades.

Closes #10

## Problem

`cargobuy` and `cargosell` (`src/vessels/vessels_trade.c`) moved gold in memory only, then wrote
the port's supply and the cargo manifest unchecked and outside any transaction. A crash before the
captain's next routine save returned a buyer's gold with the cargo recorded aboard, or lost a
seller's gold with the cargo gone; a failed manifest write left sold cargo recorded aboard, to be
sold again after a reboot.

## Fix

The shape `a703572e3` gave freight acceptance:

- `trade_record()` writes the port's supply and the manifest in one transaction and rolls back if
  either write fails. It replaces `port_adjust_supply()`, whose UPDATE is now a prepared
  statement (`vessels_trade.c`'s formatted-SQL baseline drops from 7 to 6).
- The gold moves only after that commits, and is saved with `save_char_checked()`. If the save
  fails, the gold and the hold are restored and the pre-trade supply and manifest recorded again
  with the same helper. A refused write moves no gold.
- A sale trains the crew only once it is saved.
- If the undo cannot be recorded either (review round 1), the trade stands as recorded, in memory
  too, and the persistence service's minute save stores the gold; "undone" is said only after an
  undo commits. The crash window that remains needs a settlement record and a player-file marker:
  work item #12.

## Tests

- New DB-backed `Test_vessel_cargo_trades_record_the_gold_with_the_goods`: for each command, a
  refused manifest write and a failed character save leave the gold, the hold, the manifest rows
  and the port's supply as they were (including a whole-hold sale whose emptied lot is put back);
  a saved trade moves all four.
- The contraband test's trades now save the captain, so it uses the freight test's scratch player
  files; the three trade tests share one fixture helper for their temporary tables.

## Verification

- `make test-all` with the database cases: 1,995 CuTest cases OK, the protocol harness's 32, and
  the Python suites.
- `scripts/ci/check_sql_interpolation.py`: within baseline.
- The economy live gate (`test_vessel_economy_in_game.sh`, the only gate that runs `cargobuy` and
  `cargosell`) on a fresh reload of the development dump: passed in 208 s.
- The local CI matrix (`scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`): all 33 jobs passed.

description:
Vessels study step S7 (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`, Part 5 step 7; design in 3.3.7 and 3.3.9). The plan, interpretations, ablation, decisions made while building, and verification are in the "Phase 7 (S7) progress" section.

Review range: `vessels-s7-base..vessels-s7`.

## What changes for players

- **Renown.** A hull's renown is won by sinking another player's hull: the sunk hull's weight (a boat 25, a ship 200, a warship 285), split among the hull that sank her and her grouped allies in sight. The loser drops it, and her crew lose a further 1% of their experience per 30 renown lost. NPC kills train crews but move no renown. Renown survives the wreck registry and trade-ins. `shipcrew` shows it, and `shiprenown` lists the ten most renowned hulls.
- **Prize money.** Every sinking by a player's hull pays the same sharers salvage (an eighth of the sunk hull's value scaled by what is left of her, plus half the price of each surviving weapon), a bounty of 2.5 gold per renown point above 100 (raiders now carry 150-3,000 renown), and the whole WANTED or HUNTED bounty of an owner who went down aboard, which is then cleared. It is paid through the existing settlement queue with a mail receipt.
- **Renown gates.** Able hands need 540-700 renown and veteran hands 1,350-1,640. A capital weapon needs 1,600-2,000 renown, or a veteran gunner aboard as before. Raiders scale with the quarry's renown.
- **Ship Damage Control**, an epic feat of five ranks, cuts every blow to the hull and sails of a vessel its holder owns and is aboard by 4% plus 4% per rank.
- **Contraband.** Forbidden tomes, rare poisons, and dragon eggs are each sold at one sea port, to a hull of 150, 200, or 250 renown or one with an able sailmaster and quartermaster, never to a warship or a buyer at alignment 1,000. Other ports pay their scarce price. Lawful ports' customs search hulls sailing in and seize contraband they do not stock, at Duris's odds: more likely with more units, less with renown, and much less in a full hold.
- **Cargo sales.** A seller with the SEADOG feat gets +10%, a hull under neutral colors -10%, and a warship -40%.

title: Vessels study step S6: NPC raiders, their AI, and ramming
description:
Vessels study step S6 (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`, Part 5 step 6; design in 3.3.8 and 1.6). The plan, interpretations, ablation, decisions made while building, and verification are in the "Phase 6 (S6) progress" section.

## What changes for players

- **Raiders.** A moving player's hull bigger than a boat, on open water with no lock set, is ambushed about once in 17 minutes of sailing (1 in 2002 ticks): twice as often in a pirate cove, half as often in territorial waters, and sixty times more rarely under neutral colors. Ships and transports are ambushed at most once a voyage. The hull's weight picks one of four raider tiers and a pirate or a hunter. The raider appears beyond sight off the bow and closes at full speed.
- **Raider AI** (Duris `NPCShipAI`). The basic brain turns the arc ready soonest onto the quarry and keeps within its weapons' band; the advanced brain projects both hulls 3 s ahead and works round to the quarry's weakest side with a broadside. Raiders fire as NPC return fire, ram when it pays, run when out of ammunition or holed, and board a slow quarry through the existing boarding contest. Pirates loot part of the hold and leave; hunters fight on. Killing the captain on her bridge stops her; the strongbox key is on the captain. A raider that loses her quarry leaves the sea 600 ticks later once nobody watches. Raiders cannot be claimed and never survive a restart.
- **NPC merchants** under fire now run from their attacker while returning fire, then resume their route.
- **Ramming.** `shipram [off]` braces the crew to ram the locked contact at speed 6 or more, with Duris's bow cone, chance, crash damage, fitted ram, knockdowns, and cooldowns. The sailmaster trains on every ram attempt.
- **Staff.** `vesseldebug raider <0-3> [hunter]` launches a raider against the player's hull you are aboard.

title: Vessels study S5: crew, repair and loss
description:
Vessels study step S5 (docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md, Part 5 step 5): crew, repair and loss. Review range `vessels-s5-base..vessels-s5`; review fixes go on top.

## What changes for players

- **Crew experience.** Every hired hand learns from the work (rooms sailed, reloads and shots at a locked contact, repairs, cargo sold, a hull their ship sinks) and is promoted for free on reaching the next tier. A lost hull's crew gives up about a tenth of its experience and may drop a tier, never below green. Until renown arrives (S7), mortals hire only green hands; `shipcrew` shows each hand's experience and next threshold.
- **Stamina.** Crews tire at the helm, on every shot and reload, and on repairs, and rest faster berthed or at anchor. An exhausted crew turns, accelerates, reloads and repairs more slowly and shoots less straight. `shipstatus` shows it.
- **Repair.** Repair stores (the hull weight) refill at every berth. At sea the crew mends sails, rudder and structure only up to the bosun's caps and never armor; `shiprepair` at sea is one Craft (woodworking) patch. At a shipyard `shiprepair [armor|structure|sails|rudder|weapons|all]` buys priced dock repairs that keep her at the berth. The old free repair is gone, and refits no longer repair (L10).
- **Loss (decision D3).** A player's hull that goes down is rebuilt as the shipyard's cheapest boat, stripped, and waits in the wreck registry with her name, crew, paint and permits. Insurance is automatic (75% of a merchant hull's value, 50% of the rest, 90% when an NPC sank her, nothing for a raft or a rebuilt wreck); `shipinsure` is retired and existing premiums are refunded as claims.
- **`shipsummon`** at a shipyard calls a hull, or her wreck, for a small fee after a passage time (Duris's formula, doubled from the registry, at most 75 minutes). The hull leaves at once and survives a reboot in transit.
- **Trade-in and rename.** `shipbuy <id> trade` rebuilds the owner's berthed hull as the new design for 90% of her value, keeping what of her fit-out the new class can carry. A rename after the first christening costs 10% of her value.

## Balance (D2)

Stamina lengthened the equal-warship duel from a 431 s to a 521 s median. The duel harness now reloads, tires, rests and repairs through the production ticks, and the reload lever moved from 20 s / 30 s to 17 s / 25.5 s: 1,000 duels give a 437 s median, 636 s p95, 208 s minimum, 0.7% drawn, and 437-443 s medians on four other seeds.

## Schema

title: Vessels S4: weapons and gunnery
description:
Step S4 of the DurisMUD vessel study (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`): weapons and gunnery (3.3.4, the S4 parts of 3.3.1 and 3.3.2, the default armament of 3.3.10, L6, and the S4 half of L9). The catalogue and the shipyard live in the new `src/vessels/vessels_weapons.c`, the gunnery in the new `src/vessels/vessels_gunnery.c`.

- **Catalogue:** the twelve Duris weapons (small/medium/large ballista, small/medium/large catapult, heavy ballista, light/heavy beamcannon, Mind Blast Cannon, fragmentation cannon, Long Tom) at 2 gold per platinum, plus a ram and neutral colors. Reloads were tuned by the duel harness from Duris's 30 s and 45 s to 20 s and 30 s.
- **Slots:** 16 per hull (type, arc, catalogue row, ammo, damage, reload timer: 8 bytes each, inside the 5 KiB struct budget). A new hull gets its class armament: large ballistae on a warship's bow and beams, a medium ballista on the bow of the other armed classes.
- **Class fitting (3.3.1):** hull weight, the Duris analog's mounts and weight cap per arc, and its allowed weapons. One legality check (arcs, mounts, caps, one capital weapon, the class weight budget) refuses both a purchase and a departure.
- **Shipyard:** `shipweapon list|buy|sell|swap`, `shipequip list|buy|sell`, `shiprearm [slot|all]`. A capital weapon needs a veteran gunner until renown arrives in S7. Installation and rearming keep the shipwrights at work (75 s per weight point, 75 s per weapon), which blocks departure; immortals skip it. Unowned hulls rearm when they berth.
- **Gunnery (L6):** `shiplock` a contact, then `shipfire <slot|arc>`. A shot hits on `d20 + bonus >= DC`, with `DC = 21 - round(20 * h)` and `h` Duris's `weaponsight()` chance after its 2d50 roll (crossing speed, bearing swing, closing speed with both hulls projected one second ahead through `vessel_sail_tick()`, target size, range, x1.5 miss against a hull aloft). The bonus is the gunner tier plus DEX (INT for ballistic weapons), at most +7; NPC crews fire at their tier +5. Criticals threaten by pierce; reload shortens with the gunner tier; weapons fire only on the arc facing the target and inside their range band. NPC return fire uses the same rules.
- **Battle stations (L9, 3.3.2):** a lock or a shot, fired or received, puts a crew at battle stations until 180 s after the lock clears. At battle stations a hull is refused harbors and shallows, and any other refused room rolls Duris's crash check; a grounding lands `hull weight / 25 + 1` hits.
- **Mind Blast Cannon:** a hit stuns the target crew for 5-20 s (no steering, firing, reloading, or repair); inside mid-range everyone aboard saves (Will 15) or falls prone.
- **Flight:** every vessel range counts one room per 10 Z; an airborne hull is boarded only within 10 Z; submerged hulls neither fire nor are targeted.
- **`shipsight`, `shipscan`, `contacts`:** the DC and chance per weapon against the lock; a contact's armor, structure, and weapons within 20 rooms; the arc each contact lies off and the lock.
- **Persistence (Phase 20):** every slot is a `ship_weapons` row with `catalog_id` and `ammo`; the `slot_data` blob and its hex codec are gone. Weapon rows saved before S4 load once as the class default weapon on the same arc with full ammunition, keeping their damage.
- **Duel harness (D2):** `vesseldebug balance` sails two default warships with Duris's frigate combat fit through the production movement, gunnery, damage, and reload code: 200 duels give a median of 431 s, p95 590 s, minimum 262 s, one draw (1,000: 434/604/249 s, five draws).

title: Vessels S3: the Duris damage model
description:
Step S3 of the DurisMUD vessel study (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`): the damage model (3.3.1, 3.3.3, the S3 parts of 3.3.10, and decision D6). The code lives in the new `src/vessels/vessels_damage.c`.

- **Condition profiles:** each class takes its Duris analog's per-arc armor and internal structure at the class beam armor, its sail hit points, and its price (a warship at 109: armor 87/109/65/109, structure 38/47/23/47, 140 sail, 44,000 gold). A prototype's armor (0-229) scales the profile; the shipyard price is the class price times `0.5 + 0.25 * armor / class armor + 0.25 * speed / class speed`.
- **Arcs:** the Duris bands, fore 320-40, starboard 40-140, rear 140-220, port 220-320.
- **Hits:** each fragment (every weapon resolves as a Duris ballista until S4) strikes the sails or the arc facing the shooter across its spread; armor absorbs first, confirmed criticals carry half past it, overkill spills into the structure, a gutted arc deflects one hit in three and damages weapons (disabled at 1, destroyed at 100), stern hits foul the rudder, and one structural hit in nine knocks everyone aboard prone unless they make Reflex DC 15.
- **Holes and sinking:** one holed arc (no armor, no structure) stops a hull dead at once (half speed aloft); two start the sink timer, 75-150 s for an owned hull and 1000-1500 s for an unowned one, which a restart resumes rather than rerolls. A sinking hull cannot move, fire, or be repaired. When she goes down half of each bulk cargo lot floats off as salvage crates, which `shipsalvage` hauls into a stopped hull's hold.
- **Prizes (D6):** `strikecolors`; `claimship` and `plunder` take only a beaten prize (holed, immobile, colors struck, or abandoned at sea with nobody awake aboard), and `claimship` refuses a sinking one; hostile boarding needs the target at speed 3 or less or beaten.
- **Refits:** plating and reinforcement +20%, rigging +10% speed (at least 1, at most 30), hold +25%; each costs a fifth of the class price.
- **Migration (Phase 19):** prototype armor is rescaled once by the class beam armor over the old default (`armor_scale`; a warship of 40 becomes 109). Hulls saved before S3 (`condition_model` 0) are converted once at load: the class profile at the rescaled armor, refits recomputed, and each arc, the sails, and the rudder keeping their damage fraction, with at least 1 structure per arc. `ship_runtime_state.sink_ticks` and `ship_weapons.weapon_damage` are new. The content packages write S3-scale armor and their provisioners apply Phase 19 first.
- **Display:** `shipstatus` adds structure, sails, rudder, holes, the sink timer, struck colors, and each weapon's state.

title: Vessels S2: DurisMUD movement and pacing
description:
Step S2 of the DurisMUD vessel study (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`): movement and pacing (D1).

- **Momentum:** orders set a speed and heading; every 0.5 s vessel tick the hull converges on them at its class acceleration and turn rate, scaled by the sailmaster and the rudder, and covers speed / 90 rooms (speed 10 crosses a room every 4.5 s). Its position inside the room is kept; it crosses room edges in the order its track meets them (diagonally only through a corner), and each room entered is validated; a refused room stops the hull where its track met the edge.
- **Maximum speed:** design speed times the sailmaster, load, sail-condition, and terrain/weather/lane factors, SEADOG +1 at the helm, capped at 30; the class table sets the design speeds for new prototypes.
- **Moorings:** a hull at rest in port is berthed; `undock` casts off in 30 s, the new `anchor` holds a hull at sea and `undock` weighs it in 13 s. `setsail` is now the one-room maneuver (speed 6 or less, 5 s cooldown; `up`/`down` change altitude or depth).
- **Automated movers:** the autopilot steers (comes about in place when the waypoint is astern, slows for stop waypoints, casts off by itself); hunters steer and shadow their target; merchants cruise at design speed; `setschedule` and every scheduled departure validate the route by sailing a copy of the hull through the same steering and physics. New waypoints are reached on entering their own room. A hull that comes to rest saves its runtime row. Unowned hulls get their rigging made good when they berth.
- **Removed:** the old per-tick room step, manual grounding, and the draft barrier (the 3.3.2 crash check moves to S4, the refit rescaling to S3).
- **Also fixed:** `reglist type 5` and `pathlist`, broken since `500019db1`.

title: Fix artificer devices and the artificer class
description:
Fixes the reported `device add` bug and the other 25 artificer defects listed in the work item.

## Reported bug

`device add` compared a class spell level against the circle cap, so a level 20 artificer could not add any 3rd- or 4th-circle spell. It now converts to a circle like `device create`, charges the same per-circle slot budget, and stores the assigned level.

## Other items (work item numbering)

- **1** `find_skill_num()` and `find_ability_num()` bound each copied word (stack overflow from a long spell word).
- **2** Device saves keep the DC penalty and broken flag on the existing line; old files load them as 0.
- **3** `device use` stops once the target dies or leaves the room.
- **4** Metamagic on wand/staff objects spends 1 + the metamagic cost in charges.
- **5** Improved Metamagic Science UMD check can fail; the DC comes from the spell circle.
- **6** `device create cancel` and `device repair cancel` pass the busy check.
- **7** Skills are not device spells.
- **8** Elbow Grease and Jack of All Trades reach craft, refine, harvest, brew, and golem rolls.
- **9** Artificers get the alchemist starting kit.
- **10** Construct Stone Golem at 15, Construct Iron Golem at 20.
- **11** Brilliance and Blunder is a gnome racial next to Gnomish Tinkering (existing gnomes get it on respec).
- **12, 13** The explosion applies position and death, and counts device circles.
- **14** Circle slots are assigned by trying every lower/higher choice, not greedily in typed order.
- **15, 16, 19** The dead per-device cooldown readers are removed; `device info` reads the broken flag; the free slot count is real.
- **17** Broken-device attempts and failed UMD checks take the standard action.
- **18** Build time follows the assigned levels.
- **20** A fourth spell without Brilliance and Blunder is refused.
- **21** The destroy warning says 20 minutes.
- **22** The premade artificer takes Magical Aptitude, Improved Initiative (human), and Empower Spell instead of the free craft feats.
- **23** Artificer Item Creation lets an artificer brew any spell it could put in a device, with no spell slot and ahead of the alchemist level cap; a potion takes the artificer level only for an emulated spell.
- **24** New `class-artificer` help, a rewritten `device` help, and gnome help listing both feats (dev help DB and `help.hlp`).
- **25** The slot table is clamped at level 20.

Items 10, 11, and 23 were design choices; they follow the owner's decisions, recorded in the handoff notes.

## Verification

- New `unittests/CuTest/test_artificer_devices.c` (21 tests); the device, brewing, and metamagic tests fail on the old code.
- `make test`: all suites pass.
- Local CI matrix (`scripts/ci/local/run.py`), including the clang-tidy gate: all jobs pass.
- Live check on port 4100 (private network namespace, disposable database): a new human premade artificer got the alchemist kit and the new feats; at artificer 20, `device add` took haste (3rd circle) and stone skin (4th), a four-spell create was refused, `device create cancel` worked during a build, and the new help entries display.

Handoff notes: `docs/ongoing-projects/ARTIFICER_DEVICE_FIXES.md`.

Closes #4

title: Migrate tables that older installs created before their columns existed
description:
Columns and indexes that exist only in `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` statements never reach a
database whose table already exists. A schema audit of dev and production against a fresh install

- `weather_cache.wind_speed` (read by the cyclone spell): missing on production.
- `player_save_objs.idx_name`: missing on production, so every character object load and delete

`run_legacy_table_migrations()` adds them as versioned, idempotent migrations 2026092701-03, run on
every boot. A failure is logged and retried at the next boot rather than stopping the server.
